title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Comms
author: Maya Chen
body:
Purpose

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response practice: severity definitions, detection & paging, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, game-day cadence, status page responsibilities, and customer communication templates. The goal is predictable, rapid response with blameless post-incident learning.

Scope

- Applies to all production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private control plane) and core infra components (gateway, runtime, autoscaler, routing, KV cache).
- Operational owners: eng-sre, eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime.

Incident severity and SLOs

- Severity definitions (use these when creating incident tickets and paging):
  1) Sev0 / P0 — Total outage or data loss impacting all customers or preventing any API requests. Immediate 24/7 paging.
  2) Sev1 / P1 — Major functionality degraded (e.g., >50% error rate, high tail latency causing failures for many tenants). Immediate paging.
  3) Sev2 / P2 — Partial degradation impacting a subset of customers or significant increase in errors but with viable workarounds. Business-hours paging.
  4) Sev3 / P3 — Non-urgent issues, minor bugs, or requests tracked in backlog; no paging.

- Example production SLOs (refer to /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets):
  - API availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted inference endpoints.
  - 95th percentile token latency: <= 300ms for standard models under normal load.
  - Error rate: <0.1% of requests returning 5xx for critical endpoints.

Detection & paging workflow

1) Automated detection:
   - Alerts originate from monitoring (Prometheus/Alertmanager), tracing (Jaeger), or external customer reports. Alert rules map to severity based on thresholds.
2) Immediate actions on page:
   - Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty within 5 minutes.
   - Join the incident Slack channel (#incident-<short-id>) and update the PD incident with current smoking-gun logs.
3) Initial triage script (first 15 minutes):
   - Identify scope: services, regions, customer impact.
   - Check recent deploys: CI/CD rollout windows (CI dashboard link).
   - Gather metrics: request rate, error rate, latency heatmap, GPU node health.
   - Determine next step: mitigation (rollback, scale-up, route-to-fallback) or investigation.

Escalation matrix

- 0-15 minutes: On-call engineer (primary) performs triage.
- 15-30 minutes: If unresolved or unclear root cause, notify on-call backfill + eng-sre lead.
- 30-60 minutes: Notify engineering manager and product manager for customer-facing incidents.
- >60 minutes: Alert executive on-call and Customer Success for SLA notification if necessary.

Runbook template (use as a starting point for every production service)

- Runbook header (short summary): service name, primary owner, PD escalation policy, Slack channel, runbook link.
- Symptoms: list of measurable symptoms that should trigger the runbook (e.g., 5xx > 1% over 5m, queue depth > 1000).
- Quick diagnosis steps (in order):
  1) Check health endpoints: curl https://<service>/healthz
  2) kubectl get pods -n <ns> -l app=<svc> && kubectl describe pod <pod>
  3) Check node health: /internal/tools/gpu-fleet status
  4) Tail logs: kubectl logs -f <pod> -c runtime --since=15m | grep ERROR
- Mitigation options (ranked, reversible):
  - Scale up replica count: kubectl scale deploy/<service> --replicas=+2
  - Route traffic to fallback model variant (see routing policy runbook)
  - Flush prefix cache for specific customer: POST /admin/cache/flush {customer_id}
  - Perform immediate rollback: kubectl rollout undo deploy/<service>-deployment --to-revision=<rev>
- Verification: expected observable changes and monitoring queries to validate mitigation.
- Post-incident notes: add timeline entries and link logs/trace ids.

Example runbook excerpt (service: runtime-gateway)

- Owner: eng-serving-runtime (oncall: runtime-gateway-primary)
- Symptoms: 5xx > 0.5% for > 5m OR 95th percentile token latency > 1s
- Diagnosis:
  1) Check NATS message backlog: /internal/tools/nats-stats
  2) Confirm model worker GPU health: kubectl get pods -l role=model-worker
  3) If OOMs observed, check model quantization mismatches and restart worker with Q config v2.
- Quick mitigation: reduce max-concurrent-requests on gateway config and enable `runtime.fallback=true`

Postmortem requirements (blameless, timely learning)

- Trigger: any Sev0 or Sev1 incident requires a postmortem. Sev2 may require a postmortem at manager discretion.
- Timeline: draft due within 7 calendar days; final and approved within 30 days.
- Postmortem structure (use this template in Confluence):
  1) Summary: one-paragraph user-facing explanation.
  2) Impact: timeline + affected customers, error volumes.
  3) Root cause analysis: evidence-based causal chain.
  4) Contributing factors: process or monitoring gaps.
  5) Remediation plan: short-term mitigations + long-term fixes, owners, and dates.
  6) Follow-ups: link to related PRs, runbook changes, monitoring rule updates.
- Review: technical reviewer (not author), product owner, and SRE manager must approve.

On-call rotations and responsibilities

- Rotation model: primary + secondary on-call per team (eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform). Typical cadence is 1 week.
- Handoff checklist (every rotation):
  - Confirm PagerDuty schedule accuracy.
  - Announce in #oncall with current known issues and planned maintenance.
  - Validate access: kube, cloud console, vault, and admin tooling.
  - Review outstanding incidents and follow-ups.
- Escalation ownership: clearly list PD escalation paths in the PD schedule and runbook header.

Game days (practice & resilience testing)

- Cadence: quarterly team-level game days + annual cross-team game day. Scheduling coordinated by eng-sre.
- Goals: exercise runbooks, validate SLO alerting, test rollback and fallback mechanics, and practice comms.
- Game day checklist:
  1) Pre-game: define scenario, impact, and success criteria.
  2) Inject: simulate degraded service or traffic spike using traffic-replay tool.
  3) Observe: ensure alerts fire and pagers behave as expected.
  4) Respond: teams follow runbooks, exercise escalations.
  5) Debrief: capture lessons and update runbooks/monitoring within 7 days.

Status page and customer communications

- Status page ownership: Eng-SRE owns content for platform incidents; Customer Success co-owns customer-facing messaging for account-specific incidents.
- Status categories on the page: Operational, Degraded Performance, Partial Outage, Major Outage. Update cadence: initial post within 30 minutes of incident classification; updates every 60 minutes until resolved; final post with impact summary within 24 hours.

Customer comms templates (short, use plain language)

- Initial notification (within 30 minutes):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident: <short-summary> — <status>
  Body:
  Hi <CustomerName>,

  We are investigating an issue affecting <service/region/feature>. Our engineers have identified that <high-level symptom>. We are working to mitigate and will provide updates every 60 minutes.

  Impact: <what customers see>
  Next update: <timestamp>
  Contact: <cs@redwood.example> (for account-specific concerns)

- Update template (every 60 minutes):
  Summary of progress, actions taken, and next steps.

- Resolution template (final):
  Summary of root cause, remediation steps performed, immediate mitigations, and planned long-term fixes plus links to postmortem.

Operational tooling & checklists

- Required access for on-call: PagerDuty, Slack, Confluence, Cloud Console, cluster-kubeconfig, read access to monitoring dashboards, and Vault read for secrets.
- Useful CLI snippets (store in runbook appendix):
  - Tail logs for gateway: kubectl logs -n prod -l app=gateway -c gateway --since=10m
  - Check Prometheus alert history: /internal/tools/alerts?q=<alert_name>&range=1h
  - Create incident page: /internal/tools/incidents/new?service=<svc>&sev=<sev>

Governance & continuous improvement

- Quarterly audit: eng-sre audits runbook coverage (every production service must have a runbook and owner).
- Post-incident action-tracking: all remediation actions must be converted into tracked Jira tickets with owners and due dates within 72 hours.
- Runbook freshness: owners must review runbooks after any related incident and annually at a minimum.
